title: indigo_agent_scripting: a timer created by an on-unload script can fire after the Duktape heap and the agent are freed
description:
Found 2026-11-19 in the review of d337820c (commit after 3d1f8e18f). In agent_device_detach() (indigo_drivers/agent_scripting/indigo_agent_scripting.c) the script timers are cancelled synchronously before the on-unload scripts run. A timer created by an on-unload script (indigo_set_timer / setTimeout-like binding) is therefore registered after the cancel loop and is never cancelled; it can fire after duk_destroy_heap() and after the agent device and private data are freed: a use-after-free.
Work: reproduce (integration test with an on-unload script that sets a short timer, run under ASan via the existing sanitizer targets if available, or show the callback runs after detach); fix minimally, e.g. cancel the script timers again after the on-unload scripts (and before the queue drain added in d337820c), or refuse timer creation while unloading; bump DRIVER_VERSION; document in INDIGO_SCRIPT_GUIDE.md that timers set by on-unload scripts do not run.
Also consider (same unload path, from the same review): properties that an on-unload script defines or updates on the agent itself now reach clients after the bus has already sent 'delete all properties' for the agent (indigo_bus.c indigo_detach_device), so they stay defined in clients. Either document it in the AGENT_SCRIPTING_ON_UNLOAD_SCRIPT row or suppress such updates during unload; propose the choice to the owner in a ticket note before implementing.
